thread:
Noah (sales): FYI - HarbourTech wants a POC to replace CompetitorX's /generate endpoint. Key asks: identical prompt behavior, predictable billing delta, SSO + BYOK. Can we enumerate minimal POC gates?
Leila (solutions): Minimal gates: API contract mapping, prompt-output parity tests, token accounting, security signoffs, and a rollback/fallback model.
Tobias (presales): Suggest we pick 12 representative prompts: summaries, Q&A, structured extraction, code rewrite, and some edge unicode inputs. We'll run A/B and produce per-prompt diffs.
Priya (ML Eng): Note: CompetitorX tokenizes U+2019 and some CJK combos differently. Expect small token count shifts and occasional truncation differences at high max_tokens. We'll include a variant that increases model context margin.
Cass (Security): Clarify BYOK flow: HarbourTech wants customer-managed KEK for production, but OK with platform-managed for POC. Also need SAML metadata, IP allowlist, and minimal retention policy (30d). We'll prep the security Q.
Noah (sales): HarbourTech asks whether you can keep the same response envelope shape as CompetitorX for a drop-in test.
Leila (solutions): We can add an adapter layer. Example shim (pseudo):
```
// CompetitorX reply
{"id":"r1","output":"...","usage":{"tokens":123}}
// Redwood-compatible mapping
{"request_id":"r1","choices":[{"text":"..."}],"usage":{"total_tokens":123}}
```
Tobias (presales): Acceptance criteria idea: mean token delta <= 12% on canonical set, semantic parity (human check pass rate >= 90%), latency target <= 1.5x competitor in us-west, and no new PII exposures in outputs.
Priya (ML Eng): For parity tuning we'll expose a "compat_mode" variant toggling repetition penalty and temperature to mimic competitor defaults. Document exact seed and tokenizer.
Cass (Security): Legal flagged export controls for sample prompt logs. We need DPA and data-handling addendum before sharing raw prompts externally.
infra-bot: staging cluster provisioned: harbour-poc-staging | egress IPs: 34.210.11.22, 34.210.11.23
Noah (sales): Great. HarbourTech also asked about pricing: can we offer a 60-day trial credit and a stepped committed discount for Dedicated?
Leila (solutions): Yes. Proposal: 60-day free credits up to X tokens; then 3-month ramp with 25% commit discount month2, 50% month3-4, then full commit. We'll show hosted vs dedicated unit economics.
Tobias (presales): I'll assemble a Postman collection + a small runner script to call both endpoints and output TSV: prompt,redwood_out,competitor_out,redwood_tokens,competitor_tokens,latency_ms.
Priya (ML Eng): Add model variants to the matrix: quantized-default, fp16, compat_mode. Also include a pass that forces competitor-like tokenization via pre-token rewrite for unicode edgecases.
Cass (Security): Action: I'll draft security Q answers (KMS steps, audit logs, retention, incident SLA) and check on on-prem eval options.
Noah (sales): I'll loop Legal for the DPA and schedule initial POC sync with HarbourTech (Thursday 11am PT). Action owners: @Tobias test harness, @Leila pricing writeup, @Priya variants + seed, @Cass security Q. Ping me for blockers.
Tobias (presales): Uploading the harness and sample prompts to the staging workspace now, will share link before the call.
Priya (ML Eng): Putting reproducible config in the repo (commit hash + seed).
Noah (sales): Thanks team — keeping this thread as the async source of truth.
